Company Description: Petrol d.o.o. is the Croatian subsidiary of the Ljubljana‑based Petrol Group, a leading fuel retailer and energy solutions provider in South‑East Europe. Company Description: Međunarodna zračna luka Zagreb d.d. (MZLZ) is the concessionaire that operates Franjo Tuđman Airport, Croatia’s busiest international gateway. The company is a consortium led by Aéroports de Paris and Bouygues that took over the airport in 2013 under a 30‑year public‑private partnership. MZLZ designed and built the new passenger terminal opened in 2017, which can handle over 5 million passengers annually. Core activities include airport operations, ground handling, retail and real‑estate development on the 330‑hectare site south‑east of Zagreb. More than 3,000 people work at the airport, including concessionaires, and the company plays a vital role in Croatia’s connectivity and tourism. MZLZ continues to invest in capacity, sustainability and route development to strengthen Zagreb’s position as a regional hub.

Company Description: DOK‑ING d.o.o. is a privately owned robotics and engineering company from Zagreb, globally recognised for its remotely controlled demining machines. Founded in 1992 during the Croatian War of Independence, the firm pioneered the use of unmanned vehicles to clear antipersonnel mines and unexploded ordnance. Its product range has since expanded to include emergency response robots, underground mining loaders and military C‑BRN platforms. DOK‑ING exports over 80 % of its production to customers on all continents and has vehicles deployed with UN missions, NATO forces and leading mining houses. The company employs about 300 people and runs a modern production plant in Zagreb with strong R&D capabilities. Continuous innovation and niche specialisation have positioned DOK‑ING as one of Croatia’s flagship high‑tech exporters.

Company Description: LNG Hrvatska d.o.o. is a state‑owned company established to develop and operate Croatia’s first liquefied natural gas terminal on the island of Krk. The floating storage and regasification unit (FSRU) started commercial operations in January 2021, providing annual capacity of 2.9 billion cubic metres. The terminal diversifies Croatia’s gas supply, reducing dependency on pipeline imports and enhancing energy security for the wider region. LNG Hrvatska is regulated by the Croatian Energy Regulatory Agency and offers open‑access services to shippers under EU rules. The company employs specialised engineers and maritime staff and coordinates closely with national grid operator Plinacro. Future plans include capacity upgrades and the potential integration of green hydrogen handling as part of Croatia’s energy‑transition strategy.

Company Description: Timac Agro d.o.o. is the Croatian subsidiary of French agronomy group Roullier, supplying specialised fertilisers and soil conditioners to farmers nationwide. Operating from a base near Osijek since 2011, Timac Agro combines field agronomist support with a portfolio of biostimulants and livestock nutrition products.
